name: Lake in the Hills
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lake in the Hills, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Lake in the Hills, IL: Santa at Village Hall, Flurry Fest, a holiday lights bus tour and trains nearby.
lede: Lake in the Hills does Christmas at Village Hall on Harvest Gate, where the village Parks and Recreation team brings Santa in for Flurry Fest and other small, family sized events.
celebrates: The Village of Lake in the Hills Parks and Recreation Department plans the holiday season around Village Hall at 600 Harvest Gate. Flurry Fest is the yearly Santa night there, and its theme has changed over the seasons. Younger children can hear Mrs. Claus read holiday stories at Cookies with Mr. and Mrs. Claus, and families can sign up for handwritten Letters from Santa. Residents decorate their homes for the Holiday House Decorating Contest, and a small bus carries riders around the village on the Holiday Lights Bus Tour to help judge the displays over hot chocolate and cookies.
lastyear: For the 2025 season the village's Facebook page showed Grinchmas Flurry Fest was planned for December 12 from 5 to 7 pm, promising that every Who in Who-ville would be at the fest. McHenry Life also promoted photos at Grinchmas Flurry Fest with Lake in the Hills Parks and Recreation that November. The Grinch theme went back to 2021, when the village ran Grinchmas Flurry Fest as a self-guided walk with Santa and the Grinch.
facts: Lake in the Hills began in 1923, when Federal Judge Walter J. La Buy started buying land around Woods Creek Lake, still the largest lake in the village, and had it dammed and dug out with the help of mules. The village was incorporated on November 29, 1952. Flurry Fest has taken many shapes: in 2021 its lighted Grinchmas pathway at Village Hall stayed lit in the evenings through the new year, and in 2023 it became a Frozen themed snow and ice walkway.
trains: Lake in the Hills has no Metra station of its own. The Crystal Lake and Pingree Road stations, both in neighboring Crystal Lake, are on the Union Pacific Northwest line into downtown Chicago. Metra runs decorated Holiday Trains in December, so check Metra's holiday train page for the UP Northwest schedule. For a ride with Santa closer to home, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs a holiday train, and the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs Santa's Trolley Express.
train_links: The largest railway museum in the US, with holiday train rides each season.
Historic trolley rides along the Fox River in South Elgin, plus Santa's Trolley Express.
traditions: The village's yearly Santa night at Village Hall, with a new theme most seasons, from Grinchmas to Frozen to a candy wonderland.
Cookies with Mr. and Mrs. Claus
Mrs. Claus reads holiday stories to children ages 2 to 8, with cookies, cocoa and a visit from Santa.
Residents register their decorated homes, and winners receive gift certificates and yard signs.
Riders board a village bus after hot chocolate and cookies at Village Hall and help judge the decorated houses.
Parents can sign children up to receive a handwritten letter from Santa through the village.
kidfact: When Lake in the Hills was young, workers used mules to dig out Woods Creek Lake. An island in the lake was reached by a little footbridge.
faq: What is Flurry Fest in Lake in the Hills?

Flurry Fest is the Village of Lake in the Hills' yearly Santa event at Village Hall, 600 Harvest Gate. The theme changes from year to year. It has been a Grinchmas walk with Santa and the Grinch and a Frozen snow and ice walkway, and families visit Santa for photos. Residents who pre-register usually pay less than at the door.
Does Lake in the Hills have a holiday lights tour?

Yes. The village runs a Holiday Lights Bus Tour each December. Riders meet at Village Hall for hot chocolate and cookies, then the bus leaves at 5:30 pm to tour decorated homes, and riders help judge the Holiday House Decorating Contest. Registration is required per person, and the 2026 tour already has a waitlist, so sign up early next fall.
Can kids get a letter from Santa in Lake in the Hills?

Yes. The Village of Lake in the Hills Parks and Recreation Department offers Letters from Santa. Parents register each child who would like a handwritten letter, and the village sends an email with more details after registration. Look for the program in the village's Community Pass registration catalog in the fall, since there is a sign up deadline in early December.
Where do Lake in the Hills holiday events take place?

Most village holiday events happen at Village Hall, 600 Harvest Gate. The current Village Hall was built in 2002, and its community room hosts Cookies with Mr. and Mrs. Claus while Flurry Fest fills the building. The Holiday Lights Bus Tour also starts and ends at Village Hall, with hot chocolate and cookies before the bus leaves.
